full_judgment: 4. The case of respondent-opposite party Nos.2-5 was that their father, Raj Kumar Kundu, was a physician who used to practice at Rupganj Bazar whereat he had a dispensary. The said Raj Kumar Kundu desired to purchase a property for his residential purpose. Sukumar Bose, the owner of the suit premises, offered to sell the same and the price having been fixed at Taka 3,000 (Taka three thousand) a sum of Taka 1,500 (one thousand five hundred) only had been paid to Sukumar Bose by the said Raj Kumar Kundu as earnest money in the year 1952 and the possession of the suit property was handed over to the vendee by the vendor and since then they are in possession of the suit property. On 7-4-1962 their father, Raj Kumar Kundu paid up the balance consideration money of Taka 1,500 (Taka one thousand five hundred) to Sukumar Bose and on the same date a written agreement was made between the parties. The said Sukumar Bose thereafter left for India for his treatment and died there. Thereafter the father of the respondent-opposite party Nos. 2-5 died, that they could not know about the alleged decree in Title Suit No. 132 of 1967. Sukumar Bose having not been residing at Machimdia in the year 1967 could not make any solenama as alleged by the plaintiff-appellant petitioner. The alleged solenama decree of said title suit is false, fabricated, concocted and obtained by practising fraud upon the Court. Probhabati had no right, title, interest and possession of the suit property and the alleged "Saf-Kabala" deed was forged, fictitious and without any consideration. The plaintiff-appellant petitioner did not possess the suit property at any point of time and respondent-opposite party Nos. 2-5 did not have any permissive possession under plaintiff-appellant petitioner. The further contention of the respondent opposite party Nos. 2-5 is that the respondent-opposite party No. 1 having treated them as unauthorised occupiers in the suit premises and the property in question having been declared as vested property clouds have been cast upon the right, title and interest of their property in question hence, they have been constrained to file Title Suit No. 623 of 1979 in the Court of learned Assistant Judge, Narail for declaration of their title.
